verdict.rationale: Glama publishes a documented OpenAPI 3.0.3 REST API (/v1 servers, connectors, instances, usage). It is discoverable via llms.txt and an RFC 9727 API catalog, and its hosted reference has Try-it panels, multi-language samples, and machine-readable deprecation flags, so an AI-native user can drive the directory and instance surface programmatically. The documented spec covers only that directory API: the Gateway has no REST spec and the chat product has no API evidence, so not the whole product is drivable. Missing for 10: a documented API covering the Gateway and chat surfaces, a versioning/changelog policy (changelog returns 404), documentation of undocumented prerequisites such as the credit requirement that blocked API-triggered rebuilds, and independent hands-on corroboration of API use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Glama publishes an OpenAPI 3.0.3 document for its MCP directory API
the Gateway is an MCP-protocol proxy without a separate REST spec
completing a fully machine-discoverable chain from the well-known path
alongside cURL/JavaScript/Python/PHP samples and full schemas
